implemented_requirements.requirement: Two-player Pong game with a pygame window and main loop
implemented_requirements.evidence: main.py creates a Game instance and calls Game.run(); Game.run contains the main loop with event handling, update, and draw. (main.py, game.py)

implemented_requirements.requirement: Each player controls a vertical paddle, moving up and down
implemented_requirements.evidence: Paddle class defines move() using two keys (up_key, down_key) and clamps movement; Game creates left_paddle (W/S) and right_paddle (UP/DOWN) and calls their move() each frame. (paddle.py, game.py)

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball bounces between the two paddles and off the top and bottom edges
implemented_requirements.evidence: Ball.update() moves the ball; Game.update() checks for top/bottom collision and calls Ball.bounce_off_wall(); it also checks paddle collisions and calls Ball.bounce_off_paddle(). (ball.py, game.py)

implemented_requirements.requirement: Players score a point when the opponent misses the ball
implemented_requirements.evidence: Ball.off_screen_side() detects when the ball leaves left or right; Game.update() awards a point to the opposite player via Scoreboard.award_point(). (ball.py, game.py, scoreboard.py)

WINNING_SCORE is defined in constants.py; Scoreboard.get_winner() returns a player index when a score reaches the threshold; Game.update() sets game_over when a winner exists. (constants.py, scoreboard.py, game.py)

implemented_requirements.requirement: Ball is reset and re‑served after each point
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.prepare_serve() resets ball position, stops movement, and starts a serve timer; after the timer expires Game.update() calls Ball.serve() with the appropriate direction. (game.py)

implemented_requirements.requirement: Visual rendering of paddles, ball, net, scores and win messages
implemented_requirements.evidence: Game.draw() renders background, dashed net, paddles, ball, scoreboard, and center text for ready / win messages. (game.py, paddle.py, ball.py, scoreboard.py)

judge.summary: The provided source files implement a complete two‑player Pong game meeting all core requirements: controllable paddles, ball physics with wall and paddle bounces, scoring, a configurable winning score, and automatic ball reset after each point. The game loop, rendering, and input handling are all present, and the code appears ready to run with pygame installed. No critical defects were found.
